clue.text: Musical instruments still kept in bags

indicators.note: the word for still is held inside the word for bags, as if kept in them

parts.note: sacks are bags
still in the sense of nevertheless, but

explanation.surface: Some musical instruments are still being stored in their carrying bags.
explanation.definitionFit: These are early trombones, brass instruments of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Disruption to scholars turning up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the words to and scholars are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduate scholars
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Students arriving late cause disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses TO and BAS together to give SABOT; 'on' places it above AGE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate wrecking or obstruction of work is a form of disruption.

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the following words are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Asks whether a storage place is modern or very old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the nine letters of OR ANCIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A box or vessel in which things are kept serves as a store.

clue.text: Scientist conferring youth on the French

parts.note: a youth is a boy
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A scientist bestows youthfulness on the French people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conferring ... on' reads as bestowing, but in a down entry it just stacks the youth above the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Boyle was an Anglo-Irish chemist and physicist.

clue.text: Audition comprising half-a-dozen is hardly worth thinking about

indicators.note: comprising says the word for audition holds the number inside it

parts.note: an audition is a trial performance
six in Roman numerals is VI

explanation.surface: Says an audition involving six people is barely worth bothering with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something petty or insignificant hardly merits a thought.

parts.note: Dutch courage is boldness got from drink, and the word wanted means both strong liquor and courage itself

explanation.definitionFit: Gin or whisky is a strong liquor, and boldness or mettle is also called by this word.

parts.note: a university fellow of high rank, read literally as one who professes, that is declares or affirms

explanation.definitionFit: A university academic of top rank, but literally one who professes or declares.

clue.text: Concerned with holding out, find a way

indicators.note: holding says the short word for concerning wraps round the next word

parts.note: re means concerning, about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone worried about staying out late tries to find a way home.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or course taken to reach somewhere is a path.

explanation.surface: Hosts are physicians who entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for someone's food or fun is to entertain them; doctors give medical care to patients.

clue.text: The posture for scrambling up the ascent

indicators.note: scrambling up says the letters of ascent are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Suggests the best body position for clambering up a steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of standing or holding the body is a stance or position.

clue.text: Pretty head turned by the Big Apple

indicators.note: turned says the word for head is read backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
New York's nickname, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: An attractive woman catches the eye in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for attractive or fair.

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters of reduction are made wild and rearranged

explanation.surface: Announces an incredible price cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone or something is to bring them to notice.

clue.text: When he participates in play the outcome's disastrous

definitions.text: When he participates in play the outcome's disastrous

parts.words: When he participates in play the outcome's disastrous
parts.note: an actor in tragic drama: any play he performs in ends in catastrophe for its hero

explanation.definitionFit: An actor specialising in tragic roles appears in plays with calamitous endings.

clue.text: Appearing before the court, though certainly not bent

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is an abbreviation of court

explanation.surface: A defendant in the dock appears quite honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' in the surface means crooked, as of a dishonest person; here it just means curved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright is held straight rather than curved.

explanation.surface: A soldier's bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank; blanket also means overall or all-covering, as in a blanket ban.

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
force is power

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrain a surge in electrical power.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something is to boost or augment it.

parts.note: E is short for east, so for oriental
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Describes an Asian celebration of blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring celebration of the Resurrection.

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
pensive means thoughtful

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped thinking things through is being utterly irrational.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to a price: one that is quite unreasonable is costly.
explanation.definitionFit: A costly price is one hard to justify.

clue.text: Keen to learn of financial liability being accepted by bosses

indicators.note: being accepted by says the debt goes inside the word for bosses

parts.note: bosses are studs, raised knobs on a surface
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: Describes an eager student who has heard about money owed and accepted by managers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bosses' looks like managers but means knobs or studs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish person devoted to study is eager for knowledge.

indicators.note: receiving says the word for force takes the next letter inside

parts.note: to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: A military force receives an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Commendation or acclaim is offered as a tribute.

clue.text: "Ever against ———— cares, lap me in soft Lydian airs" (Milton)

definitions.text: "Ever against ———— cares, lap me in soft Lydian airs" (Milton)

parts.words: "Ever against ———— cares, lap me in soft Lydian airs" (Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's poem L'Allegro with one word left out, the word meaning gnawing or consuming

explanation.definitionFit: Milton's line speaks of gnawing, consuming worries, the missing word meaning devouring.

parts.note: a low protective wall or rail found along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony; the surface suggests someone ranting when nervous

explanation.definitionFit: A low wall or barrier along the edge of a roof or bridge.

clue.text: The colour intended, say, by the Empress of Blandings

parts.note: the Empress of Blandings is Lord Emsworth's prize pig in P G Wodehouse's Blandings stories

indicators.note: say signals that the word for intended is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: Asks what shade Wodehouse's prize sow had in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places PIG first; MENT sounds like MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that gives paint or skin its colouring.

parts.note: read as eaves dropping: something hanging down from the eaves of a roof in freezing weather, not secret listening

explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of frozen water forms on eaves in freezing weather.

indicators.note: is here reads as has, the word for cook having the unit within it

parts.note: a chef is a cook
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Praises the cook of a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks like a military unit but is I, the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal or foremost, standing out above the rest.

clue.text: Popular pet as it may be, it's really not suitable

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: as it may be suggests the letters of pet in any order they may fall

explanation.surface: Says a fashionable pet may be a poor choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it may be' rearranges PET as EPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy or inappropriate, unfit for the purpose.

clue.text: Get screwed up, drunk, and need to be thrown out

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters of need are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone gets confused and drunk and needs ejecting.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut or screw turned firmly in has been made fast.

clue.text: Buckle in pain and get a check-up

annotationWithheld.why: Buckle in pain and get a check-up (5): TACHE (buckle) contains ACHE (pain), but no clue word gives T, and the forward run in 'get a check' cannot use the separated 'in' as its indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Buckle in pain and get a check-up

parts.note: not a guest bedroom but space left over, the margin between two objects

explanation.definitionFit: The gap or margin allowed between objects, as under a bridge.

indicators.note: about says the abbreviation for company goes round the word for publish

parts.note: to air is to make public, broadcast

explanation.surface: A firm is about to issue its funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' seems to be money but is a capital city, Egypt's.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt's capital city.

explanation.surface: A dramatic warning that the route has no exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a way in, the opposite of an exit; also a main dish of a meal.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the cattle word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: steers are young bullocks, cattle
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Drovers move cattle along without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who guide a vehicle or herd direct it.
